summary: Milestone 2026.09.599 completed 13 experiments in 9.6 minutes, including 3 compute-bound experiments. The 8.15-minute Three-family isomorphic fixed-sequence compatibility stream dominated elapsed time, while the locked compute-task GPU-idle indicator remained false.
bottlenecks_identified: Three-family isomorphic fixed-sequence compatibility stream was the main elapsed-time bottleneck at 8.15 minutes; no data available this milestone identifies the costly phase.
Three-family forced-sequence scoring admission canary was the next-longest listed compute-bound experiment at 1.25 minutes; no data available this milestone explains its duration.
Disk-mtime reconstruction ranks experiment durations but does not expose phase costs or bind accelerator samples to each compute task.
The GPU monitor identifies batching multiple questions per forward pass as a throughput opportunity for the single Python inference process.
improvements_suggested: Add configurable batches of 8-16 questions per forward pass for eligible single-model inference work.
Record task-owned phase timings and task-window GPU samples for every compute-bound launch.
Emit loaded-model count and runner identity in each launch receipt; use both GPUs only when 2 or more model workloads are ready in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Implement configurable 8-16 question batching on the single-model inference path.
Instrument the fixed-sequence compatibility stream with phase clocks and task-scoped accelerator telemetry.
Add launch receipts that record model concurrency, device placement, and runner selection.
meta_reflection: The evidence can rank elapsed time but cannot diagnose the longest run because phase timing is not tied to task-window GPU samples. Future records should capture loaded-model count and runner selection so correct single-model placement can be distinguished from unused parallel capacity.
